newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks rise to fresh highs on Dow, poll.
newsitem.headline: French stocks rise to fresh highs on Dow, poll.

text.p: French stocks rose to an all time high above 2,800 points on Friday morning, bolstered by a record close on Wall Street and a fresh poll showing the conservatives leading in the parliamentary election.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 16.22 points, or 0.58 percent, at 2,792.23 at 1000 GMT, while the CAC-40 May futures contract rose 18 points to 2,787.
Volume was a brisk 1.49 billion francs.

The market was encouraged by Wall Street's first close above 7,300 points and higher bond prices. In addition, an Ipsos poll for the magazine Le Point projected the ruling RPR-UDF coalition would win 323 seats in the 577-member National Assembly, up from 290 in a similar poll last week.
The poll indicated the Socialists would trail with 226 seats.
Surveys by other polling institutes have shown even clearer leads for the centre-right in recent days.
But some traders worry the market may be going overboard, as polls also show Prime Minister Alain Juppe enjoys little support. "He's the only one pushing real reform," one broker said.
The CAC eased from a session high of 2,800.84 as some players grew cautious ahead of a three-day weekend.

Shares in Danone rose 2.41 percent to 933 francs, extending their recent advance on bullish meetings with shareholders and analysts. The group forecast higher 1997 results and said it planned a listing in New York.
Shares in electrical equipment supplier Schneider slumped 5.16 percent to 319.70 francs after the company said it planned strategic acquisitions and reported flat first-quarter sales.
